name: Scapular elevation
description: Superior translation of scapula and clavicular elevation.

fields.Movement: Superior translation of scapula and clavicular elevation.

name: Scapular depression
description: Inferior scapular movement; active muscle contribution depends on task and fixation.

fields.Movement: Inferior scapular movement; active muscle contribution depends on task and fixation.

name: Scapular protraction
description: Scapula travels anterolaterally around the thoracic wall.

fields.Movement: Scapula travels anterolaterally around the thoracic wall.

name: Scapular retraction
description: Scapula travels posteromedially toward the vertebral column.

fields.Movement: Scapula travels posteromedially toward the vertebral column.

name: Scapular upward rotation
description: Glenoid turns superiorly; inferior angle moves laterally. Upper/lower trapezius and lower serratus form a force couple.

fields.Movement: Glenoid turns superiorly; inferior angle moves laterally. Upper/lower trapezius and lower serratus form a force couple.

name: Scapular downward rotation
description: Glenoid turns inferiorly as the arm is lowered.

fields.Movement: Glenoid turns inferiorly as the arm is lowered.

name: Shoulder flexion
description: Arm moves anteriorly; predominantly a transverse axis.

fields.Movement: Arm moves anteriorly; predominantly a transverse axis.

name: Shoulder extension
description: Arm moves posteriorly. Sternocostal pectoralis major can extend a flexed arm.

fields.Movement: Arm moves posteriorly. Sternocostal pectoralis major can extend a flexed arm.

name: Shoulder abduction
description: Supraspinatus contributes early and throughout elevation. Deltoid provides increasing torque; full elevation requires scapular upward rotation.

fields.Movement: Supraspinatus contributes early and throughout elevation. Deltoid provides increasing torque; full elevation requires scapular upward rotation.

name: Shoulder adduction
description: Arm moves toward the trunk from an abducted position.

fields.Movement: Arm moves toward the trunk from an abducted position.

name: Shoulder medial rotation
description: Humerus rotates inward about its longitudinal axis.

fields.Movement: Humerus rotates inward about its longitudinal axis.

name: Shoulder lateral rotation
description: Humerus rotates outward about its longitudinal axis.

fields.Movement: Humerus rotates outward about its longitudinal axis.

name: Shoulder circumduction
description: Sequential flexion, abduction, extension and adduction; not a separate independent joint axis.

fields.Movement: Sequential flexion, abduction, extension and adduction; not a separate independent joint axis.

name: Elbow flexion
description: Forearm approaches the arm around the elbow flexion axis; biceps contribution depends on forearm position.

fields.Movement: Forearm approaches the arm around the elbow flexion axis; biceps contribution depends on forearm position.

name: Elbow extension
description: Forearm straightens at the elbow.

fields.Movement: Forearm straightens at the elbow.

name: Pronation
description: Radius crosses anterior to ulna as the palm turns posteriorly from anatomical position. Distal radius and hand rotate around the ulnar head; ulna is relatively stable.

fields.Movement: Radius crosses anterior to ulna as the palm turns posteriorly from anatomical position. Distal radius and hand rotate around the ulnar head; ulna is relatively stable.

name: Supination
description: Radius and ulna become parallel. Palm faces anteriorly in anatomical position; with flexed elbow, palm faces upward.

fields.Movement: Radius and ulna become parallel. Palm faces anteriorly in anatomical position; with flexed elbow, palm faces upward.

name: Wrist flexion
description: Palm approaches anterior forearm.

fields.Movement: Palm approaches anterior forearm.

name: Wrist extension
description: Dorsum approaches posterior forearm.

fields.Movement: Dorsum approaches posterior forearm.

name: Radial deviation
description: Hand moves toward the radial / thumb side.

fields.Movement: Hand moves toward the radial / thumb side.

name: Ulnar deviation
description: Hand moves toward the ulnar / little-finger side.

fields.Movement: Hand moves toward the ulnar / little-finger side.

name: Finger MCP flexion
description: Intrinsic muscles flex MCP joints while the extensor expansion permits simultaneous IP extension.

fields.Movement: Intrinsic muscles flex MCP joints while the extensor expansion permits simultaneous IP extension.

name: Finger MCP extension
description: Long extensors extend MCP joints.

fields.Movement: Long extensors extend MCP joints.

name: Finger IP flexion
description: FDS flexes PIP; FDP flexes DIP. Both can assist more proximal flexion.

fields.Movement: FDS flexes PIP; FDP flexes DIP. Both can assist more proximal flexion.

name: Finger IP extension
description: Lumbricals and interossei act through the extensor expansion; function depends on MCP posture and tendon balance.

fields.Movement: Lumbricals and interossei act through the extensor expansion; function depends on MCP posture and tendon balance.

name: Finger abduction
description: DAB: dorsal interossei abduct digits from the middle-finger axis.

fields.Movement: DAB: dorsal interossei abduct digits from the middle-finger axis.

name: Finger adduction
description: PAD: palmar interossei adduct digits toward the middle-finger axis.

fields.Movement: PAD: palmar interossei adduct digits toward the middle-finger axis.

name: Thumb flexion
description: CMC flexion moves thumb across the palm; FPL flexes IP, FPB mainly MCP.

fields.Movement: CMC flexion moves thumb across the palm; FPL flexes IP, FPB mainly MCP.

name: Thumb extension
description: Thumb moves away from the palm in its plane; EPL extends IP, EPB mainly MCP.

fields.Movement: Thumb moves away from the palm in its plane; EPL extends IP, EPB mainly MCP.

name: Thumb abduction
description: Palmar abduction moves perpendicular to palm; radial abduction is in the palm plane. These should not be confused.

fields.Movement: Palmar abduction moves perpendicular to palm; radial abduction is in the palm plane. These should not be confused.

name: Thumb adduction
description: Returns thumb toward plane and side of the palm.

fields.Movement: Returns thumb toward plane and side of the palm.

name: Thumb opposition
description: Combined abduction, flexion and medial rotation of first metacarpal; fingertip pads face one another.

fields.Movement: Combined abduction, flexion and medial rotation of first metacarpal; fingertip pads face one another.

name: Thumb reposition
description: Reverse coupled movement returning the thumb from opposition.

fields.Movement: Reverse coupled movement returning the thumb from opposition.

name: Winged scapula
description: Medial border prominence, accentuated during a wall push; impaired scapular upward rotation limits overhead elevation.

fields.Mechanism: Long thoracic neuropathy weakens serratus anterior; the medial border lifts from the thorax.
fields.Clinical presentation: Medial border prominence, accentuated during a wall push; impaired scapular upward rotation limits overhead elevation.
fields.Distinguish from: Normal serratus holds scapula against thorax. Trapezius palsy can produce a different winging pattern.

mechanism: Long thoracic neuropathy weakens serratus anterior; the medial border lifts from the thorax.
presentation: Medial border prominence, accentuated during a wall push; impaired scapular upward rotation limits overhead elevation.
comparison: Normal serratus holds scapula against thorax. Trapezius palsy can produce a different winging pattern.

name: Wrist drop
description: Wrist and finger extension weakness; sensory and triceps deficits depend on lesion level.

fields.Mechanism: Radial lesion proximal enough to denervate wrist extensors leaves unopposed wrist flexion.
fields.Clinical presentation: Wrist and finger extension weakness; sensory and triceps deficits depend on lesion level.
fields.Distinguish from: Axilla: triceps may be weak. Radial groove: triceps usually spared. PIN: finger/thumb drop with preserved, often radially deviated wrist extension and no cutaneous deficit.

mechanism: Radial lesion proximal enough to denervate wrist extensors leaves unopposed wrist flexion.
presentation: Wrist and finger extension weakness; sensory and triceps deficits depend on lesion level.
comparison: Axilla: triceps may be weak. Radial groove: triceps usually spared. PIN: finger/thumb drop with preserved, often radially deviated wrist extension and no cutaneous deficit.

name: Ulnar claw
description: MCP hyperextension with PIP and DIP flexion in ring and little fingers.

fields.Mechanism: Loss of intrinsic MCP flexion and IP extension in digits 4–5 allows extensor/flexor imbalance.
fields.Clinical presentation: MCP hyperextension with PIP and DIP flexion in ring and little fingers.
fields.Distinguish from: Distal lesions may claw more. Proximal lesions also weaken medial FDP, reducing DIP flexion: the ulnar paradox.

mechanism: Loss of intrinsic MCP flexion and IP extension in digits 4–5 allows extensor/flexor imbalance.
presentation: MCP hyperextension with PIP and DIP flexion in ring and little fingers.
comparison: Distal lesions may claw more. Proximal lesions also weaken medial FDP, reducing DIP flexion: the ulnar paradox.

name: Thenar wasting and loss of opposition
description: Thenar flattening and thumb lying more in the plane of the palm; sometimes called an ape-thumb appearance.

fields.Mechanism: Denervation of median-innervated thenar muscles weakens palmar abduction and opposition.
fields.Clinical presentation: Thenar flattening and thumb lying more in the plane of the palm; sometimes called an ape-thumb appearance.
fields.Distinguish from: Isolated recurrent branch injury can spare sensation. Adductor pollicis remains ulnar-innervated.

mechanism: Denervation of median-innervated thenar muscles weakens palmar abduction and opposition.
presentation: Thenar flattening and thumb lying more in the plane of the palm; sometimes called an ape-thumb appearance.
comparison: Isolated recurrent branch injury can spare sensation. Adductor pollicis remains ulnar-innervated.

name: Carpal tunnel syndrome
description: Paresthesia in lateral 3½ digits; advanced motor involvement can weaken thenar muscles.

fields.Mechanism: Median nerve compression beneath flexor retinaculum.
fields.Clinical presentation: Paresthesia in lateral 3½ digits; advanced motor involvement can weaken thenar muscles.
fields.Distinguish from: Thenar-eminence skin sensation is usually spared because palmar cutaneous branch travels superficial to retinaculum.

mechanism: Median nerve compression beneath flexor retinaculum.
presentation: Paresthesia in lateral 3½ digits; advanced motor involvement can weaken thenar muscles.
comparison: Thenar-eminence skin sensation is usually spared because palmar cutaneous branch travels superficial to retinaculum.

name: Anterior interosseous syndrome
description: Abnormal tip-to-tip OK pinch, using flattened finger pads.

fields.Mechanism: AIN motor dysfunction impairs thumb IP and index DIP flexion.
fields.Clinical presentation: Abnormal tip-to-tip OK pinch, using flattened finger pads.
fields.Distinguish from: No cutaneous sensory loss. Distinguish from carpal tunnel and isolated tendon rupture.

mechanism: AIN motor dysfunction impairs thumb IP and index DIP flexion.
presentation: Abnormal tip-to-tip OK pinch, using flattened finger pads.
comparison: No cutaneous sensory loss. Distinguish from carpal tunnel and isolated tendon rupture.

name: Hand of benediction
description: Index and middle fingers fail to flex normally while ring/little fingers can flex via ulnar-innervated FDP.

fields.Mechanism: Proximal median lesion impairs flexion of thumb and especially index/middle fingers during an attempted fist.
fields.Clinical presentation: Index and middle fingers fail to flex normally while ring/little fingers can flex via ulnar-innervated FDP.
fields.Distinguish from: An examination sign during attempted flexion, not a resting posture. Pattern varies with incomplete lesions and tendon interconnections.

mechanism: Proximal median lesion impairs flexion of thumb and especially index/middle fingers during an attempted fist.
presentation: Index and middle fingers fail to flex normally while ring/little fingers can flex via ulnar-innervated FDP.
comparison: An examination sign during attempted flexion, not a resting posture. Pattern varies with incomplete lesions and tendon interconnections.

name: Erb-Duchenne palsy
description: Classical posture: adducted, medially rotated shoulder with extended elbow and pronated forearm.

fields.Mechanism: Upper-trunk injury chiefly involving C5–C6 weakens abductors, lateral rotators, elbow flexors and supinators.
fields.Clinical presentation: Classical posture: adducted, medially rotated shoulder with extended elbow and pronated forearm.
fields.Distinguish from: Severity and hand posture vary with the extent of plexus injury.

mechanism: Upper-trunk injury chiefly involving C5–C6 weakens abductors, lateral rotators, elbow flexors and supinators.
presentation: Classical posture: adducted, medially rotated shoulder with extended elbow and pronated forearm.
comparison: Severity and hand posture vary with the extent of plexus injury.

name: Klumpke palsy
description: Intrinsic hand weakness with possible clawing involving more digits than an isolated ulnar lesion.

fields.Mechanism: Lower-trunk C8–T1 injury weakens intrinsic hand muscles and selected long flexors.
fields.Clinical presentation: Intrinsic hand weakness with possible clawing involving more digits than an isolated ulnar lesion.
fields.Distinguish from: Horner syndrome suggests associated proximal T1 sympathetic involvement; it is not obligatory.

mechanism: Lower-trunk C8–T1 injury weakens intrinsic hand muscles and selected long flexors.
presentation: Intrinsic hand weakness with possible clawing involving more digits than an isolated ulnar lesion.
comparison: Horner syndrome suggests associated proximal T1 sympathetic involvement; it is not obligatory.

name: Anterior shoulder dislocation
description: Loss of normal shoulder contour and restricted movement; possible lateral-shoulder sensory deficit.

fields.Mechanism: Humeral head moves anteroinferiorly relative to glenoid, commonly after abduction and external rotation.
fields.Clinical presentation: Loss of normal shoulder contour and restricted movement; possible lateral-shoulder sensory deficit.
fields.Distinguish from: Axillary nerve is at risk; neurovascular findings depend on displacement and associated injury.

mechanism: Humeral head moves anteroinferiorly relative to glenoid, commonly after abduction and external rotation.
presentation: Loss of normal shoulder contour and restricted movement; possible lateral-shoulder sensory deficit.
comparison: Axillary nerve is at risk; neurovascular findings depend on displacement and associated injury.

name: Supraspinatus tendinopathy
description: Pain with resisted abduction and an often-described mid-range painful arc.

fields.Mechanism: Degenerative and load-related change in supraspinatus tendon may cause pain on elevation.
fields.Clinical presentation: Pain with resisted abduction and an often-described mid-range painful arc.
fields.Distinguish from: Painful arc is not specific to one diagnosis; mechanisms can involve tendon and subacromial bursa.

mechanism: Degenerative and load-related change in supraspinatus tendon may cause pain on elevation.
presentation: Pain with resisted abduction and an often-described mid-range painful arc.
comparison: Painful arc is not specific to one diagnosis; mechanisms can involve tendon and subacromial bursa.

name: Rotator cuff tear
description: Pain and weakness; larger tears may impair active elevation despite better passive range.

fields.Mechanism: Partial or full-thickness disruption of one or more cuff tendons compromises force transmission and dynamic stability.
fields.Clinical presentation: Pain and weakness; larger tears may impair active elevation despite better passive range.
fields.Distinguish from: Not every tear produces the same movement deficit; location and extent matter.

mechanism: Partial or full-thickness disruption of one or more cuff tendons compromises force transmission and dynamic stability.
presentation: Pain and weakness; larger tears may impair active elevation despite better passive range.
comparison: Not every tear produces the same movement deficit; location and extent matter.

name: Subacromial pain / impingement
description: Pain during elevation, often approximately 60–120° but highly variable.

fields.Mechanism: Pain associated with the subacromial region can involve rotator cuff and bursa, with multiple contributing mechanisms.
fields.Clinical presentation: Pain during elevation, often approximately 60–120° but highly variable.
fields.Distinguish from: Do not model all cases as a bone mechanically crushing a normal tendon.

mechanism: Pain associated with the subacromial region can involve rotator cuff and bursa, with multiple contributing mechanisms.
presentation: Pain during elevation, often approximately 60–120° but highly variable.
comparison: Do not model all cases as a bone mechanically crushing a normal tendon.

name: Proximal biceps tendon rupture
description: Possible Popeye bulge with pain, bruising and reduced supination endurance.

fields.Mechanism: Long-head tendon rupture releases proximal tension and may permit distal displacement of muscle belly.
fields.Clinical presentation: Possible Popeye bulge with pain, bruising and reduced supination endurance.
fields.Distinguish from: A distal biceps rupture has different anatomy and functional consequences. No fabricated bulge geometry is supplied.

mechanism: Long-head tendon rupture releases proximal tension and may permit distal displacement of muscle belly.
presentation: Possible Popeye bulge with pain, bruising and reduced supination endurance.
comparison: A distal biceps rupture has different anatomy and functional consequences. No fabricated bulge geometry is supplied.

name: Lateral epicondylitis
description: Lateral elbow pain provoked by gripping or resisted wrist extension.

fields.Mechanism: Common extensor tendinopathy, often centered on ECRB origin.
fields.Clinical presentation: Lateral elbow pain provoked by gripping or resisted wrist extension.
fields.Distinguish from: Usually a tendinopathy rather than purely acute inflammation.

mechanism: Common extensor tendinopathy, often centered on ECRB origin.
presentation: Lateral elbow pain provoked by gripping or resisted wrist extension.
comparison: Usually a tendinopathy rather than purely acute inflammation.

name: Medial epicondylitis
description: Medial elbow pain with resisted wrist flexion or pronation.

fields.Mechanism: Flexor-pronator origin tendinopathy at medial epicondyle.
fields.Clinical presentation: Medial elbow pain with resisted wrist flexion or pronation.
fields.Distinguish from: Ulnar nerve lies nearby posterior to medial epicondyle; paresthesia suggests additional nerve involvement.

mechanism: Flexor-pronator origin tendinopathy at medial epicondyle.
presentation: Medial elbow pain with resisted wrist flexion or pronation.
comparison: Ulnar nerve lies nearby posterior to medial epicondyle; paresthesia suggests additional nerve involvement.

name: De Quervain tenosynovitis
description: Radial styloid pain associated with thumb movement.

fields.Mechanism: Stenosing tendon-sheath disorder in first dorsal extensor compartment.
fields.Clinical presentation: Radial styloid pain associated with thumb movement.
fields.Distinguish from: APL and EPB are implicated; EPL runs in the third compartment.

mechanism: Stenosing tendon-sheath disorder in first dorsal extensor compartment.
presentation: Radial styloid pain associated with thumb movement.
comparison: APL and EPB are implicated; EPL runs in the third compartment.

name: Mallet finger
description: DIP flexion with loss of active DIP extension.

fields.Mechanism: Terminal extensor mechanism disruption, sometimes with avulsion fracture.
fields.Clinical presentation: DIP flexion with loss of active DIP extension.
fields.Distinguish from: PIP posture is not the defining primary feature.

mechanism: Terminal extensor mechanism disruption, sometimes with avulsion fracture.
presentation: DIP flexion with loss of active DIP extension.
comparison: PIP posture is not the defining primary feature.

name: Boutonniere deformity
description: PIP flexion with DIP hyperextension.

fields.Mechanism: Central slip disruption permits volar migration of lateral bands over time.
fields.Clinical presentation: PIP flexion with DIP hyperextension.
fields.Distinguish from: Distinguish from swan-neck: the PIP/DIP directions are reversed.

mechanism: Central slip disruption permits volar migration of lateral bands over time.
presentation: PIP flexion with DIP hyperextension.
comparison: Distinguish from swan-neck: the PIP/DIP directions are reversed.

name: Swan-neck deformity
description: PIP hyperextension with DIP flexion.

fields.Mechanism: Extensor-flexor imbalance and PIP volar restraint insufficiency; multiple causes.
fields.Clinical presentation: PIP hyperextension with DIP flexion.
fields.Distinguish from: This is a pattern, not one unique lesion.

mechanism: Extensor-flexor imbalance and PIP volar restraint insufficiency; multiple causes.
presentation: PIP hyperextension with DIP flexion.
comparison: This is a pattern, not one unique lesion.

name: Surgical neck fracture
description: Possible deltoid weakness and sensory loss over lateral shoulder.

fields.Mechanism: Fracture near structures winding around the surgical neck.
fields.Clinical presentation: Possible deltoid weakness and sensory loss over lateral shoulder.
fields.Distinguish from: Neurovascular injury is a risk, not an inevitable consequence.

mechanism: Fracture near structures winding around the surgical neck.
presentation: Possible deltoid weakness and sensory loss over lateral shoulder.
comparison: Neurovascular injury is a risk, not an inevitable consequence.

name: Midshaft humeral fracture
description: Possible wrist/finger extension weakness; triceps is commonly spared.

fields.Mechanism: Radial nerve and profunda brachii lie close to the humeral shaft in the radial groove.
fields.Clinical presentation: Possible wrist/finger extension weakness; triceps is commonly spared.
fields.Distinguish from: Deficit depends on fracture and nerve injury level.

mechanism: Radial nerve and profunda brachii lie close to the humeral shaft in the radial groove.

name: Supracondylar humeral fracture
description: Possible brachial artery compromise and median/AIN dysfunction.

fields.Mechanism: Distal humeral fracture, commonly extension type, can threaten anterior neurovascular structures.
fields.Clinical presentation: Possible brachial artery compromise and median/AIN dysfunction.
fields.Distinguish from: Different displacement patterns can injure radial or ulnar nerve; do not assign one nerve to every pattern.

name: Medial epicondyle fracture
description: Possible medial-digit paresthesia and intrinsic weakness.

fields.Mechanism: Ulnar nerve passes posterior to the epicondyle and may be stretched or entrapped.
fields.Clinical presentation: Possible medial-digit paresthesia and intrinsic weakness.
fields.Distinguish from: Association depends on displacement and elbow injury.

name: Scaphoid fracture
description: Snuffbox tenderness; proximal fragment has risk of nonunion and avascular necrosis.

fields.Mechanism: Waist fracture can interrupt retrograde intraosseous supply to proximal pole.
fields.Clinical presentation: Snuffbox tenderness; proximal fragment has risk of nonunion and avascular necrosis.
fields.Distinguish from: Initial radiographs can be unrevealing. Risk varies with fracture location and displacement.

mechanism: Waist fracture can interrupt retrograde intraosseous supply to proximal pole.
presentation: Snuffbox tenderness; proximal fragment has risk of nonunion and avascular necrosis.

name: Colles fracture
description: Dorsal dinner-fork profile in a displaced classic pattern.

fields.Mechanism: Classic distal radial fracture with dorsal displacement/angulation of distal fragment.
fields.Clinical presentation: Dorsal dinner-fork profile in a displaced classic pattern.
fields.Distinguish from: Compare with volar displacement of Smith fracture. A bone fracture line requires a segmented asset.

mechanism: Classic distal radial fracture with dorsal displacement/angulation of distal fragment.
presentation: Dorsal dinner-fork profile in a displaced classic pattern.
comparison: Compare with volar displacement of Smith fracture. A bone fracture line requires a segmented asset.

name: Smith fracture
description: Volar deformity in the displaced classic pattern.

fields.Mechanism: Classic distal radial fracture with volar displacement/angulation of distal fragment.
fields.Clinical presentation: Volar deformity in the displaced classic pattern.
fields.Distinguish from: Opposite displacement direction to classic Colles.

mechanism: Classic distal radial fracture with volar displacement/angulation of distal fragment.
presentation: Volar deformity in the displaced classic pattern.
comparison: Opposite displacement direction to classic Colles.

name: Monteggia fracture-dislocation
description: Loss of normal proximal radioulnar/radiocapitellar alignment.

fields.Mechanism: Ulnar fracture with radial-head dislocation; direction varies by injury type.
fields.Clinical presentation: Loss of normal proximal radioulnar/radiocapitellar alignment.

mechanism: Ulnar fracture with radial-head dislocation; direction varies by injury type.
presentation: Loss of normal proximal radioulnar/radiocapitellar alignment.
comparison: Classic anterior radial-head dislocation is one type, not all Monteggia injuries.

name: Galeazzi fracture-dislocation
description: Distal forearm pain with disturbed distal radioulnar alignment.

fields.Mechanism: Radial shaft fracture with DRUJ disruption.
fields.Clinical presentation: Distal forearm pain with disturbed distal radioulnar alignment.
fields.Distinguish from: Distinguish from Monteggia, which involves ulna and radial-head dislocation.

mechanism: Radial shaft fracture with DRUJ disruption.
presentation: Distal forearm pain with disturbed distal radioulnar alignment.

name: Clavicle fracture
